main_issue: Whether Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling salted fish in the shared kitchen, and what rule or arrangement (e.g. Saturdays only) the household should adopt.

A-B.evidence: B backs A's complaint (T8 'He's right', T15); T22 B rejects A's Saturday proposal because of laundry, and A accepts that in T24.

A-C.evidence: C complains about laundry smell (T3) and rejects the Saturday plan (T23); A concedes 'Saturdays won't work' (T24).

A-D.evidence: D resists restrictions (T6, T16, T18); A softens to 'nobody says you can't cook' and offers Saturdays (T17, T19), but D still raises objections (T20).

B-C.evidence: Both complain about the smell in their clothes and laundry; C echoes B's point 'she's right' (T23) on the Saturday plan.

B-D.evidence: B says the smell sticks to fabrics (T8, T15); D asks 'So because there are three of you, I cannot cook?' (T16); D's laundry point (T20) is echoed by B (T22), but B still wants the smell gone.

C-D.evidence: C complains about laundry (T3) and says the smell persists on any day (T23); D cites their laundry (T20) only to reject the Saturday plan, while still defending cooking.
